---
title: "Read the conversation"
description: "Follow what the Assistant is doing as it works: its replies, its tool calls, the questions it asked, and why it stopped."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The transcript in the Assistant tab shows everything that happens in a conversation: your messages, the replies, each tool call, each question, and what went wrong. Reading it tells you what the Assistant did and why it stopped.

<AtAGlance
  menu="View ▸ Assistant"
  keys="⌃⌘A"
  where="Inspector ▸ Assistant tab"
  needs="Your own Anthropic API key"
/>

## What's in the transcript

| You see | It looks like |
| --- | --- |
| Your message | Semibold |
| The Assistant's [replies](#replies) | Regular |
| Its [working notes](#working-notes) | Small and faint |
| [Tool call lines](#tool-call-lines), [`failed:` lines](#failed-lines), [permission lines](#permission-lines) and [notes](#notes) | Small monospace |
| [Errors](#errors) | Red |

## Replies

A reply streams in as it's written, under your message. The transcript scrolls to the newest line each time anything arrives, even if you've scrolled up to read something earlier.

Replies are short on purpose. See [How it behaves](/assistant/what-it-can-do/#how-it-behaves).

## Working notes

Between tool calls the Assistant writes small, faint notes on what it's working through. They're its thinking updates, and they stream in as replies do. They aren't addressed to you, and there's nothing to answer.

## Tool call lines

Each tool call is one line, with the tool's name and its arguments:

```
split (at: 1200000, clips: [12])
```

That line splits clip 12 two seconds in. A time shows as a large number, 600,000 to the second.

Arguments are in alphabetical order, and the line shows only their first 70 characters. A call with no arguments shows the tool's name alone.

The line appears when the call starts. A call that works adds nothing more to the transcript, and you see its result in the project. A call that doesn't work adds a [`failed:` line](#failed-lines). [All tools](/mcp/tools/) describes every tool.

## `failed:` lines

A tool call that didn't work is followed by `failed:` and the reason. The line shows the first 200 characters of the answer.

The Assistant reads the same answer, so it can correct itself. A `failed:` line followed by another tool call is normal, and often the next try works.

| The line reads | What happened |
| --- | --- |
| `failed:` and a sentence about the edit | Frame Job wouldn't make the edit. The sentence is the same one you'd see yourself. See [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/). |
| `failed: The person declined: …` | You chose **Deny**, or the question was declined for you. The Assistant won't try that call again this turn unless you ask. |
| `failed: Cancelled by the user.` | **Stop** cancelled the call before it started. See [Stop a turn](/assistant/stop-a-turn/). |
| `failed: … is not available to the assistant: …` | The Assistant isn't allowed that tool. The reason names the menu item to use instead. See [What it won't do](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/). |

## Permission lines

The Assistant [asks before it writes a file](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/). Once a question is answered, the transcript records the outcome with the question's sentence, for example `Allowed: export writes /Users/you/Movies/cut.mp4`.

| The line starts | What happened |
| --- | --- |
| `Allowed:` | You chose **Allow**. |
| `Declined:` | You chose **Deny**. |
| `Declined (stop):` | You chose **Stop** while the question was waiting. |
| `Declined (close):` | The conversation ended while the question was waiting, for example because the key or the model changed. |
| `Declined (helper):` | [The helper stopped](#if-the-helper-stops) while the question was waiting. |

## Notes

Frame Job writes its own small monospace notes into the transcript.

| The note reads | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| `Cost: …` | What the turn came to, at the end of each turn. For example, `Cost: $0.0312 · Frame Job's estimate at LiteLLM prices (cached 2026-11-02)`. See [What it costs](/assistant/cost/). |
| `Compacting the conversation (… tokens)…` | The conversation has passed your compaction threshold, and Frame Job is replacing it with a summary. See [Long conversations](/assistant/context-and-compaction/). |
| `Compacted: … → about … tokens. Earlier renders are gone; the assistant re-renders when it needs to look.` | The summary is in place. |
| `Compaction didn't finish (…); it will try again after the next turn.` | No summary came back, so the conversation is unchanged. |
| `Cleared … old tool results (… tokens) from the model's view.` | Old results were dropped from what the model sees. This only happens with clearing turned on in Settings. |
| `The model is now …; the next message starts a new conversation.` | The model changed in Settings. |
| `The API key changed; the next message starts a new conversation.` | The key was saved or removed in Settings. |
| `The spend ledger … could not be written: ….` | A response's cost couldn't be recorded. The note appears once per conversation, and an unrecorded response is missing from the month's total in Settings. |

## Errors

An error is a red line, and it says what went wrong.

| The error reads | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| `API error status: message` | Anthropic refused or failed the request, for example a bad key, a rate limit or an outage. The status is Anthropic's, and it's blank when the request never reached Anthropic. |
| "The reply was cut off at the output limit." | The response reached 32,000 tokens. Thinking counts toward that as well as the reply. |
| "The model declined this request." | The model wouldn't do what you asked. |
| "The assistant helper stopped. Clear the conversation to start a new one." | See [If the helper stops](#if-the-helper-stops). |

If a conversation can't start, for example because there's no key, the reason shows as an error and your message stays in the field.

A request you end with **Stop** shows no error.

## Automatic retries

Rate limits, outages and connection failures are retried up to three times before an error appears. Nothing shows in the transcript during a retry, so a turn can seem to pause. A bad key fails at once.

## Select and copy

The transcript is one block of text, so you can drag a selection across entries. <kbd>⌘C</kbd> copies it as plain text, with a line break between entries.

A conversation isn't saved with the project. Copy anything you want to keep before you close the window.

## If the helper stops

The helper is the background program that talks to Anthropic for the Assistant. If it stops:

- The transcript says "The assistant helper stopped. Clear the conversation to start a new one."
- A question that was waiting is declined, with a `Declined (helper):` line.
- The edits the Assistant already made stay in the project.

Your next message starts a new conversation under the old transcript. The Assistant doesn't remember anything from before, and the Spend row carries on from where it was. To start clean, choose **Clear** (↺) at the top of the tab.

## Good to know

- A turn takes at most 30 rounds of tool calls. At that point it ends with no error line, and your next message carries on from there.
- Each window has its own transcript. **Clear** empties it, and closing the window ends it. See [Chat with the Assistant](/assistant/chat/).

## Related

- [Chat with the Assistant](/assistant/chat/)
- [What it won't do and what it asks first](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/)
- [Stop a turn](/assistant/stop-a-turn/)
- [Long conversations](/assistant/context-and-compaction/)
- [What it costs](/assistant/cost/)

---
title: "What the Assistant can do"
description: "What you can ask the Assistant for, job by job, how it checks its work, and where its limits are."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The Assistant edits the project in its own window. You ask in plain words, it makes the edits one at a time, and each one lands where you can see it and undo it.

<AtAGlance
  menu="View ▸ Assistant"
  keys="⌃⌘A"
  where="Inspector ▸ Assistant tab"
  tools={['get_project', 'render_frame', 'undo', 'redo']}
  needs="Your own Anthropic API key"
/>

## The same tools as MCP

The Assistant works through the same tools an agent uses [over MCP](/mcp/overview/), so anything here is something an agent can do too. There are a few exceptions, listed in [What it won't do](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/), and it asks you first before some tools that write files.

Four tools are always at hand: reading the project, rendering a frame, undo and redo. It finds every other tool by searching for what it wants to do, so you never need to name one. It never sees a tool that's withheld from it.

Each job below lists its tools, because those are the names you'll see in the [tool call lines](/assistant/conversation/#tool-call-lines). [All tools](/mcp/tools/) describes each one.

## What you can ask for

### Projects and navigation

It can open, create and save projects, move the playhead, set the in and out range, change the selection, and enter or leave a nest. It can also make a [new project from a range](/projects/new-project-from-range/) or a [vertical version](/framing/make-vertical-version/).

Saving asks first. Making a new project from a range or a vertical version asks first when it names where to save. Moving the playhead, setting the range and changing the selection aren't edits, so they make no undo step.

A project it opens or creates gets a window of its own, and the Assistant stays with the project it started in.

<AtAGlance tools={['open_project', 'new_project', 'new_project_from_range', 'make_vertical_version', 'save_project', 'set_playhead', 'set_range', 'set_selection', 'set_scope']} />

### Tracks, markers and the canvas

It can add, remove and reorder tracks, remove the empty ones, rename a track, and set a track's switches, [matte](/canvas/matte-tracks/) and [mix](/audio/track-volume-and-pan/). It can add, move, rename and remove [markers](/timeline/markers/), make one a chapter, and set its colour, which you can't do yourself. It can change the canvas's [size](/projects/canvas-size/), [frame rate](/projects/frame-rate/) and [background](/projects/background-and-timecode/).

<AtAGlance tools={['add_track', 'remove_track', 'move_track', 'set_track', 'remove_empty_tracks', 'add_marker', 'set_marker', 'remove_marker', 'set_canvas']} />

### Media

It can [import](/projects/import-media/), [relink](/projects/relink-media/) and [remove](/projects/remove-media/) media, [copy it into the project](/projects/consolidate-media/) and set a file's [camera log](/hdr/camera-log/). Copying into the project asks first.

It can also save where a file's speech is, read the [on-device analysis](/projects/media-analysis/) of a file, and attach or read a recording's [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/).

<AtAGlance tools={['import_media', 'add_media', 'relink_media', 'remove_media', 'set_media_color', 'set_media_speech', 'consolidate_media', 'get_media_analysis', 'set_media_cursor', 'get_cursor_events']} />

### Placing clips

It can place media, [text](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/), [shapes](/text-and-shapes/shape-clips/), [backgrounds](/canvas/backgrounds/), [adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/) and [graphics](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/). It can [insert and overwrite](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/), paste and duplicate, and put [text behind a subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/).

<AtAGlance tools={['add_clip', 'add_text_clip', 'add_shape_clip', 'add_adjustment_clip', 'add_background', 'add_blurred_background', 'text_behind_subject', 'insert_clip', 'overwrite_clip', 'paste', 'duplicate', 'insert_graphic']} />

### Editing clips

It can [move](/editing/move-clips/), [trim](/editing/trimming/), [split](/editing/splitting/), [slip and roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/), [rate-stretch](/speed/rate-stretch/), [ripple-delete and lift](/editing/delete-clips/), [insert time and close gaps](/editing/close-gaps/). It can [detach audio and attach it again](/audio/detach-and-attach/) and make [J-cuts and L-cuts](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/).

For several cameras or long recordings it can [split at shot changes](/editing/split-at-shot-changes/), [copy pieces to another track](/multicam/copy-pieces/), [switch a shot's angle](/multicam/switch-angle/) and [switch by speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/).

<AtAGlance tools={['move_clip', 'trim_start', 'trim_end', 'rate_stretch', 'slip', 'roll', 'split', 'delete', 'ripple_delete', 'ripple_delete_range', 'ripple_delete_ranges', 'lift_range', 'insert_time', 'close_gap', 'detach_audio', 'attach_audio', 'split_at_shots', 'copy_pieces', 'switch_angle', 'switch_by_speaker']} />

### Nests

It can [nest clips](/editing/nests/) or take a nest apart. An edit goes where the window is looking unless the Assistant names a nest, and it can enter a nest as you do. Markers belong to the timeline, never to a nest.

<AtAGlance tools={['nest', 'unnest']} />

### Speed

It can [set a clip's speed](/speed/change-speed/), [reverse a clip](/speed/reverse/), [freeze a frame](/speed/freeze-frame/), add [speed ramps](/speed/make-a-ramp/), [retime a range](/speed/retime-range/) and [speed up the typing](/recording/speed-up-typing/) in a screen recording.

<AtAGlance tools={['set_speed', 'set_reversed', 'freeze_frame', 'add_speed_ramp', 'retime_range', 'speed_up_typing']} />

### Look and sound

It can change how a clip looks and sounds: position, scale, crop, colour, filters, volume, fades, text and its style, and shapes. It can rename or label a clip, turn its picture or sound off, and [paste attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/).

It can also work with [transitions](/motion/transitions/), [actions](/motion/actions/) and [zooms](/motion/zoom-to-region/), including [Auto Zoom](/recording/auto-zoom/), and with [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/), [camera layouts](/framing/camera-layouts/) and [reframing](/framing/reframe-clip/).

<AtAGlance tools={['set_video', 'set_audio', 'set_text', 'set_shape', 'set_clip', 'set_enabled', 'paste_attributes', 'analyze_cutout', 'add_transition', 'set_transition', 'set_transition_duration', 'set_transition_style', 'add_action', 'add_zoom_action', 'auto_zoom', 'switch_layout', 'reframe_clip', 'set_action', 'set_action_end', 'remove_action']} />

### Captions and words

It can [import captions](/captions/import-captions/), [transcribe on this Mac](/captions/on-device-transcription/), read a clip's or the whole timeline's timed words, [re-lay word captions](/captions/re-lay-captions/) for the canvas, and [export captions](/captions/export-captions/).

Transcribing runs on this Mac only, because the Assistant can't send audio to the cloud. Exporting captions asks first.

<AtAGlance tools={['import_captions', 'transcribe', 'get_transcript', 'get_timeline_transcript', 'relay_captions', 'export_captions']} />

### Audio clean-up

It can find [silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) and [filler words](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/), [normalize](/audio/normalize/) loudness, [enhance a voice](/audio/enhance-voice/), [match one clip's sound to another](/audio/match-audio/) and [synchronize audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/).

<AtAGlance tools={['detect_silence', 'detect_fillers', 'normalize_clip', 'enhance_voice', 'match_audio', 'sync_audio']} />

### Graphics

It can write, change, place, render, rename, delete, restore, export and import graphics, import their fonts and pictures, and add [shortcut overlays](/recording/shortcut-overlays/). Exporting a graphic asks first. See [Graphics with an agent](/graphics/agents-and-graphics/#the-assistant).

<AtAGlance tools={['add_graphic_clip', 'set_graphic', 'write_graphic', 'get_graphic', 'graphic_reference', 'render_graphic', 'import_graphic_font', 'import_graphic_asset', 'delete_graphic', 'rename_graphic', 'restore_graphic', 'list_graphics', 'insert_graphic', 'export_graphic', 'import_graphic', 'add_shortcut_overlays']} />

### Export

It can [export](/export/export-sheet/), check how an export is going, or cancel it. Exporting asks first, because it writes a movie and replaces any file already there.

<AtAGlance tools={['export', 'export_status', 'cancel_export']} />

## Cut words by asking

You can ask the Assistant to take out filler words, silences or a false start. It cuts each request as one undo step, labelled **Ripple Delete**.

It can only find filler words in media that already has a cloud transcript made with them, and it can't upload audio to make one. In other media it cuts nothing, and it reports which media has no such transcript. To start the paid transcription, use [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/) yourself.

It removes a false start only when you ask, because deciding what counts as one is a judgement of meaning. It says which words it will cut, then cuts them. There's no menu command for this.

See [Cut false starts](/cleanup/false-starts/).

## It looks at rendered frames

The Assistant checks its work by rendering a frame of the finished timeline, drawn the way an export draws it. It's told to look before and after a visual edit. It renders at the playhead unless it picks a time, and it keeps the image small.

Rendering writes a picture file without asking. By default that's a temporary file.

:::note
The frames it renders go to Anthropic, along with your messages and the project's details. See [Assistant privacy](/assistant/privacy/).
:::

Earlier renders don't survive compaction, so it renders again when it needs to look. See [Long conversations](/assistant/context-and-compaction/).

## Each edit is an undo step

Every edit the Assistant makes is its own undo step on the project, the same as your own, and **Edit ▸ Undo** names it after the edit. A turn isn't grouped, so a turn that made ten edits takes ten undos.

To take back its last change, press <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> outside the message field. You can also ask the Assistant to undo or redo.

## How it behaves

- **Short replies.** A reply is a sentence or two, and it doesn't repeat what the tool lines already show.
- **Captions only on request.** It writes or restyles a caption only when you ask.
- **Medium effort, thinking on.** This is fixed, and Settings has no control for it. The faint [working notes](/assistant/conversation/#working-notes) are its thinking updates.

## Only its own window's project

title: "What the Assistant can do"
description: "What you can ask the Assistant for, job by job, how it checks its work, and where its limits are."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The Assistant edits the project in its own window. You ask in plain words, it makes the edits one at a time, and each one lands where you can see it and undo it.

<AtAGlance
  menu="View ▸ Assistant"
  keys="⌃⌘A"
  where="Inspector ▸ Assistant tab"
  tools={['get_project', 'render_frame', 'undo', 'redo']}
  needs="Your own Anthropic API key"
/>

## The same tools as MCP

The Assistant works through the same tools an agent uses [over MCP](/mcp/overview/), so anything here is something an agent can do too. There are a few exceptions, listed in [What it won't do](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/), and it asks you first before some tools that write files.

Four tools are always at hand: reading the project, rendering a frame, undo and redo. It finds every other tool by searching for what it wants to do, so you never need to name one. It never sees a tool that's withheld from it.

Each job below lists its tools, because those are the names you'll see in the [tool call lines](/assistant/conversation/#tool-call-lines). [All tools](/mcp/tools/) describes each one.

## What you can ask for

### Projects and navigation

It can open, create and save projects, move the playhead, set the in and out range, change the selection, and enter or leave a nest. It can also make a [new project from a range](/projects/new-project-from-range/) or a [vertical version](/framing/make-vertical-version/).

Saving asks first. Making a new project from a range or a vertical version asks first when it names where to save. Moving the playhead, setting the range and changing the selection aren't edits, so they make no undo step.

A project it opens or creates gets a window of its own, and the Assistant stays with the project it started in.

<AtAGlance tools={['open_project', 'new_project', 'new_project_from_range', 'make_vertical_version', 'save_project', 'set_playhead', 'set_range', 'set_selection', 'set_scope']} />

### Tracks, markers and the canvas

It can add, remove and reorder tracks, remove the empty ones, rename a track, and set a track's switches, [matte](/canvas/matte-tracks/) and [mix](/audio/track-volume-and-pan/). It can add, move, rename and remove [markers](/timeline/markers/), make one a chapter, and set its colour, which you can't do yourself. It can change the canvas's [size](/projects/canvas-size/), [frame rate](/projects/frame-rate/) and [background](/projects/background-and-timecode/).

<AtAGlance tools={['add_track', 'remove_track', 'move_track', 'set_track', 'remove_empty_tracks', 'add_marker', 'set_marker', 'remove_marker', 'set_canvas']} />

### Media

It can [import](/projects/import-media/), [relink](/projects/relink-media/) and [remove](/projects/remove-media/) media, [copy it into the project](/projects/consolidate-media/) and set a file's [camera log](/hdr/camera-log/). Copying into the project asks first.

It can also save where a file's speech is, read the [on-device analysis](/projects/media-analysis/) of a file, and attach or read a recording's [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/).

<AtAGlance tools={['import_media', 'add_media', 'relink_media', 'remove_media', 'set_media_color', 'set_media_speech', 'consolidate_media', 'get_media_analysis', 'set_media_cursor', 'get_cursor_events']} />

### Placing clips

It can place media, [text](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/), [shapes](/text-and-shapes/shape-clips/), [backgrounds](/canvas/backgrounds/), [adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/) and [graphics](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/). It can [insert and overwrite](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/), paste and duplicate, and put [text behind a subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/).

It can [move](/editing/move-clips/), [trim](/editing/trimming/), [split](/editing/splitting/), [slip and roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/), [rate-stretch](/speed/rate-stretch/), [ripple-delete and lift](/editing/delete-clips/), [insert time and close gaps](/editing/close-gaps/). It can [nest clips](/editing/nests/) or take a nest apart. An edit goes where the window is looking unless the Assistant names a nest, and it can enter a nest as you do. Markers belong to the timeline, never to a nest.

<AtAGlance tools={['set_speed', 'set_reversed', 'freeze_frame', 'add_speed_ramp', 'retime_range', 'speed_up_typing']} />

### Look and sound

It can change how a clip looks and sounds: position, scale, crop, colour, filters, volume, fades, text and its style, and shapes. It can rename or label a clip, turn its picture or sound off, and [paste attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/).

It can [import captions](/captions/import-captions/), [transcribe on this Mac](/captions/on-device-transcription/), read a clip's or the whole timeline's timed words, [re-lay word captions](/captions/re-lay-captions/) for the canvas, and [export captions](/captions/export-captions/).

It can [export](/export/export-sheet/), check how an export is going, or cancel it. Exporting asks first, because it writes a movie and replaces any file already there.

You can ask the Assistant to take out filler words, silences or a false start. It cuts each request as one undo step, labelled **Ripple Delete**.

---
title: "Read the conversation"
description: "Follow what the Assistant is doing as it works: its replies, its tool calls, the questions it asked, and why it stopped."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The transcript in the Assistant tab shows everything that happens in a conversation: your messages, the replies, each tool call, each question, and what went wrong. Reading it tells you what the Assistant did and why it stopped.

<AtAGlance
  menu="View ▸ Assistant"
  keys="⌃⌘A"
  where="Inspector ▸ Assistant tab"
  needs="Your own Anthropic API key"
/>

## What's in the transcript

| You see | It looks like |
| --- | --- |
| Your message | Semibold |
| The Assistant's [replies](#replies) | Regular |
| Its [working notes](#working-notes) | Small and faint |
| [Tool call lines](#tool-call-lines), [`failed:` lines](#failed-lines), [permission lines](#permission-lines) and [notes](#notes) | Small monospace |
| [Errors](#errors) | Red |

## Replies

A reply streams in as it's written, under your message. The transcript scrolls to the newest line each time anything arrives, even if you've scrolled up to read something earlier.

Replies are short on purpose. See [How it behaves](/assistant/what-it-can-do/#how-it-behaves).

## Working notes

Between tool calls the Assistant writes small, faint notes on what it's working through. They're its thinking updates, and they stream in as replies do. They aren't addressed to you, and there's nothing to answer.

## Tool call lines

Each tool call is one line, with the tool's name and its arguments:

```
split (at: 1200000, clips: [12])
```

That line splits clip 12 two seconds in. A time shows as a large number, 600,000 to the second.

Arguments are in alphabetical order, and the line shows only their first 70 characters. A call with no arguments shows the tool's name alone.

The line appears when the call starts. A call that works adds nothing more to the transcript, and you see its result in the project. A call that doesn't work adds a [`failed:` line](#failed-lines). [All tools](/mcp/tools/) describes every tool.

## `failed:` lines

A tool call that didn't work is followed by `failed:` and the reason. The line shows the first 200 characters of the answer.

The Assistant reads the same answer, so it can correct itself. A `failed:` line followed by another tool call is normal, and often the next try works.

| The line reads | What happened |
| --- | --- |
| `failed:` and a sentence about the edit | Frame Job wouldn't make the edit. The sentence is the same one you'd see yourself. See [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/). |
| `failed: The person declined: …` | You chose **Deny**, or the question was declined for you. The Assistant won't try that call again this turn unless you ask. |
| `failed: Cancelled by the user.` | **Stop** cancelled the call before it started. See [Stop a turn](/assistant/stop-a-turn/). |
| `failed: … is not available to the assistant: …` | The Assistant isn't allowed that tool. The reason names the menu item to use instead. See [What it won't do](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/). |

## Permission lines

The Assistant [asks before it writes a file](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/). Once a question is answered, the transcript records the outcome with the question's sentence, for example `Allowed: export writes /Users/you/Movies/cut.mp4`.

| The line starts | What happened |
| --- | --- |
| `Allowed:` | You chose **Allow**. |
| `Declined:` | You chose **Deny**. |
| `Declined (stop):` | You chose **Stop** while the question was waiting. |
| `Declined (close):` | The conversation ended while the question was waiting, for example because the key or the model changed. |
| `Declined (helper):` | [The helper stopped](#if-the-helper-stops) while the question was waiting. |

## Notes

Frame Job writes its own small monospace notes into the transcript.

| The note reads | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| `Cost: …` | What the turn came to, at the end of each turn. For example, `Cost: $0.0312 · Frame Job's estimate at LiteLLM prices (cached 2026-11-02)`. See [What it costs](/assistant/cost/). |
| `Compacting the conversation (… tokens)…` | The conversation has passed your compaction threshold, and Frame Job is replacing it with a summary. See [Long conversations](/assistant/context-and-compaction/). |
| `Compacted: … → about … tokens. Earlier renders are gone; the assistant re-renders when it needs to look.` | The summary is in place. |
| `Compaction didn't finish (…); it will try again after the next turn.` | No summary came back, so the conversation is unchanged. |
| `Cleared … old tool results (… tokens) from the model's view.` | Old results were dropped from what the model sees. This only happens with clearing turned on in Settings. |
| `The model is now …; the next message starts a new conversation.` | The model changed in Settings. |
| `The API key changed; the next message starts a new conversation.` | The key was saved or removed in Settings. |
| `The spend ledger … could not be written: ….` | A response's cost couldn't be recorded. The note appears once per conversation, and an unrecorded response is missing from the month's total in Settings. |

## Errors

An error is a red line, and it says what went wrong.

| The error reads | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| `API error status: message` | Anthropic refused or failed the request, for example a bad key, a rate limit or an outage. The status is Anthropic's, and it's blank when the request never reached Anthropic. |
| "The reply was cut off at the output limit." | The response reached 32,000 tokens. Thinking counts toward that as well as the reply. |
| "The model declined this request." | The model wouldn't do what you asked. |
| "The assistant helper stopped. Clear the conversation to start a new one." | See [If the helper stops](#if-the-helper-stops). |

If a conversation can't start, for example because there's no key, the reason shows as an error and your message stays in the field.

A request you end with **Stop** shows no error.

## Automatic retries

Rate limits, outages and connection failures are retried up to three times before an error appears. Nothing shows in the transcript during a retry, so a turn can seem to pause. A bad key fails at once.

## Select and copy

The transcript is one block of text, so you can drag a selection across entries. <kbd>⌘C</kbd> copies it as plain text, with a line break between entries.

A conversation isn't saved with the project. Copy anything you want to keep before you close the window.

## If the helper stops

The helper is the background program that talks to Anthropic for the Assistant. If it stops:

- The transcript says "The assistant helper stopped. Clear the conversation to start a new one."
- A question that was waiting is declined, with a `Declined (helper):` line.
- The edits the Assistant already made stay in the project.

Your next message starts a new conversation under the old transcript. The Assistant doesn't remember anything from before, and the Spend row carries on from where it was. To start clean, choose **Clear** (↺) at the top of the tab.

## Good to know

- A turn takes at most 30 rounds of tool calls. At that point it ends with no error line, and your next message carries on from there.
- Each window has its own transcript. **Clear** empties it, and closing the window ends it. See [Chat with the Assistant](/assistant/chat/).

## Related

- [Chat with the Assistant](/assistant/chat/)
- [What it won't do and what it asks first](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/)
- [Stop a turn](/assistant/stop-a-turn/)
- [Long conversations](/assistant/context-and-compaction/)
- [What it costs](/assistant/cost/)

<AtAGlance tools={['import_media', 'add_media', 'relink_media', 'remove_media', 'set_media_color', 'set_media_speech', 'consolidate_media', 'get_media_analysis', 'set_media_cursor', 'get_cursor_events']} />

### Placing clips

It can place media, [text](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/), [shapes](/text-and-shapes/shape-clips/), [backgrounds](/canvas/backgrounds/), [adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/) and [graphics](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/). It can [insert and overwrite](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/), paste and duplicate, and put [text behind a subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/).

<AtAGlance tools={['add_clip', 'add_text_clip', 'add_shape_clip', 'add_adjustment_clip', 'add_background', 'add_blurred_background', 'text_behind_subject', 'insert_clip', 'overwrite_clip', 'paste', 'duplicate', 'insert_graphic']} />

### Editing clips

It can [move](/editing/move-clips/), [trim](/editing/trimming/), [split](/editing/splitting/), [slip and roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/), [rate-stretch](/speed/rate-stretch/), [ripple-delete and lift](/editing/delete-clips/), [insert time and close gaps](/editing/close-gaps/). It can [detach audio and attach it again](/audio/detach-and-attach/) and make [J-cuts and L-cuts](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/).

For several cameras or long recordings it can [split at shot changes](/editing/split-at-shot-changes/), [copy pieces to another track](/multicam/copy-pieces/), [switch a shot's angle](/multicam/switch-angle/) and [switch by speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/).

<AtAGlance tools={['move_clip', 'trim_start', 'trim_end', 'rate_stretch', 'slip', 'roll', 'split', 'delete', 'ripple_delete', 'ripple_delete_range', 'ripple_delete_ranges', 'lift_range', 'insert_time', 'close_gap', 'detach_audio', 'attach_audio', 'split_at_shots', 'copy_pieces', 'switch_angle', 'switch_by_speaker']} />

### Nests

It can [nest clips](/editing/nests/) or take a nest apart. An edit goes where the window is looking unless the Assistant names a nest, and it can enter a nest as you do. Markers belong to the timeline, never to a nest.

<AtAGlance tools={['nest', 'unnest']} />

### Speed

It can [set a clip's speed](/speed/change-speed/), [reverse a clip](/speed/reverse/), [freeze a frame](/speed/freeze-frame/), add [speed ramps](/speed/make-a-ramp/), [retime a range](/speed/retime-range/) and [speed up the typing](/recording/speed-up-typing/) in a screen recording.

<AtAGlance tools={['set_speed', 'set_reversed', 'freeze_frame', 'add_speed_ramp', 'retime_range', 'speed_up_typing']} />

### Look and sound

It can change how a clip looks and sounds: position, scale, crop, colour, filters, volume, fades, text and its style, and shapes. It can rename or label a clip, turn its picture or sound off, and [paste attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/).

It can also work with [transitions](/motion/transitions/), [actions](/motion/actions/) and [zooms](/motion/zoom-to-region/), including [Auto Zoom](/recording/auto-zoom/), and with [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/), [camera layouts](/framing/camera-layouts/) and [reframing](/framing/reframe-clip/).

<AtAGlance tools={['set_video', 'set_audio', 'set_text', 'set_shape', 'set_clip', 'set_enabled', 'paste_attributes', 'analyze_cutout', 'add_transition', 'set_transition', 'set_transition_duration', 'set_transition_style', 'add_action', 'add_zoom_action', 'auto_zoom', 'switch_layout', 'reframe_clip', 'set_action', 'set_action_end', 'remove_action']} />

### Captions and words

It can [import captions](/captions/import-captions/), [transcribe on this Mac](/captions/on-device-transcription/), read a clip's or the whole timeline's timed words, [re-lay word captions](/captions/re-lay-captions/) for the canvas, and [export captions](/captions/export-captions/).

Transcribing runs on this Mac only, because the Assistant can't send audio to the cloud. Exporting captions asks first.

<AtAGlance tools={['import_captions', 'transcribe', 'get_transcript', 'get_timeline_transcript', 'relay_captions', 'export_captions']} />

### Audio clean-up

It can find [silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) and [filler words](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/), [normalize](/audio/normalize/) loudness, [enhance a voice](/audio/enhance-voice/), [match one clip's sound to another](/audio/match-audio/) and [synchronize audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/).

<AtAGlance tools={['detect_silence', 'detect_fillers', 'normalize_clip', 'enhance_voice', 'match_audio', 'sync_audio']} />

### Graphics

It can write, change, place, render, rename, delete, restore, export and import graphics, import their fonts and pictures, and add [shortcut overlays](/recording/shortcut-overlays/). Exporting a graphic asks first. See [Graphics with an agent](/graphics/agents-and-graphics/#the-assistant).

<AtAGlance tools={['add_graphic_clip', 'set_graphic', 'write_graphic', 'get_graphic', 'graphic_reference', 'render_graphic', 'import_graphic_font', 'import_graphic_asset', 'delete_graphic', 'rename_graphic', 'restore_graphic', 'list_graphics', 'insert_graphic', 'export_graphic', 'import_graphic', 'add_shortcut_overlays']} />

### Export

It can [export](/export/export-sheet/), check how an export is going, or cancel it. Exporting asks first, because it writes a movie and replaces any file already there.

<AtAGlance tools={['export', 'export_status', 'cancel_export']} />

## Cut words by asking

You can ask the Assistant to take out filler words, silences or a false start. It cuts each request as one undo step, labelled **Ripple Delete**.

It can only find filler words in media that already has a cloud transcript made with them, and it can't upload audio to make one. In other media it cuts nothing, and it reports which media has no such transcript. To start the paid transcription, use [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/) yourself.

It removes a false start only when you ask, because deciding what counts as one is a judgement of meaning. It says which words it will cut, then cuts them. There's no menu command for this.

See [Cut false starts](/cleanup/false-starts/).

## It looks at rendered frames

The Assistant checks its work by rendering a frame of the finished timeline, drawn the way an export draws it. It's told to look before and after a visual edit. It renders at the playhead unless it picks a time, and it keeps the image small.

Rendering writes a picture file without asking. By default that's a temporary file.

:::note
The frames it renders go to Anthropic, along with your messages and the project's details. See [Assistant privacy](/assistant/privacy/).
:::

Earlier renders don't survive compaction, so it renders again when it needs to look. See [Long conversations](/assistant/context-and-compaction/).

## Each edit is an undo step

Every edit the Assistant makes is its own undo step on the project, the same as your own, and **Edit ▸ Undo** names it after the edit. A turn isn't grouped, so a turn that made ten edits takes ten undos.

To take back its last change, press <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> outside the message field. You can also ask the Assistant to undo or redo.

## How it behaves

- **Short replies.** A reply is a sentence or two, and it doesn't repeat what the tool lines already show.
- **Captions only on request.** It writes or restyles a caption only when you ask.
- **Medium effort, thinking on.** This is fixed, and Settings has no control for it. The faint [working notes](/assistant/conversation/#working-notes) are its thinking updates.

## Only its own window's project

The Assistant acts only on the project in its own window, and each window has its own conversation. If a tool call names another project, it fails with a line such as "The assistant edits its own window's project, Trailer; Interview is a different project."

If its project is no longer open, a call answers that the Assistant's project is no longer open.

## Limits

- It works only on the project in its own window.
- It needs your own Anthropic API key. There's no Frame Job account. See [Set up the Assistant](/assistant/set-up/).
- It can't record the screen, close its window's project, or send audio to the cloud transcriber.
- A tool call that arrives during a drag waits until you release the mouse.
- **Stop** doesn't cancel an export that's already been queued. See [Stop a turn](/assistant/stop-a-turn/).
- With compaction off, a long conversation eventually fails until you **Clear** it.
- Changing the key or the model ends every window's conversation.
